steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Is one city really faster?** in *Confidence intervals by bootstrap*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.explain: A resample has the same size and only contains values from the data, so its mean can never leave the data's range.

steps.title: Rebuild Is one city really faster? cold
prompt: Delivery times (minutes) from two cities are arrays `a` and `b`. Write `diff_ci(a, b, rng, reps=3000)` that bootstraps the **difference in medians** `median(a) - median(b)`: in each repetition resample `a` and `b` separately (with replacement, own sizes) and take the difference.

Return `(lo, hi, verdict)` where `lo, hi` are the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles rounded to 1 decimal (plain floats) and `verdict` is `"a slower"` if `lo > 0`, `"a faster"` if `hi < 0`, else `"no clear difference"`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
